label: FICTION. Six invented role-change episodes. Every person, system, ticket, date and record below was written to exercise the review method. Nobody is described, and no row is an observation of anything real.

cases.summary: Contractor departure at end of engagement
cases.notes: The case the order names. The central identity account was confirmed disabled; the deployment pipeline carries a separate local account that nobody has looked at. An aggregate 'access removed' would have hidden that entirely.

access_changes.entitlement: local pipeline account, created outside the identity provider

evidence.statement: A published standard requires access removal on the last working day
Offboarding ticket raised by the engaging manager
Offboarding approved by the engaging manager
Ticket closed, marked account disabled
Directory export shows the account in a disabled state
Ticket closed, marked repository access removed

interview_prompts: For this departure, which systems were in scope, and who decided the list?
How are accounts created outside the identity provider brought into offboarding?
Can you show the pipeline's own account listing as at a date after 31 August?

cases.person_role: Moved from application support to release engineering (fictional)
cases.summary: Changed responsibilities: new access granted, previous access not evidenced as removed
cases.notes: The second case the order names. Movers are where entitlement accumulates: the grant is confirmed because somebody needed it to work, and the revoke has a request and nothing after it.

access_changes.entitlement: tier 2 support role, no longer required

evidence.statement: A published standard requires entitlements to follow role changes
Release approver role approved by the receiving manager
Role assigned
Pipeline role listing shows the release approver role present
Request raised to remove the tier 2 support role

interview_prompts: When somebody changes team, what triggers the removal of the entitlements they no longer need?
Is the removal tracked to completion, or closed when the new access is working?
Can you show the support console's role listing for this person as at any date after 1 July?

cases.notes: The comparatively clean case. Both systems observed after the change; included so the matrix is not only failures.

evidence.statement: Onboarding request raised
Approved by the hiring manager
Account created
Directory export shows an enabled account
Repository access approved by the repository owner
Repository collaborator export shows write access

interview_prompts: How soon after a start date is access checked against what was approved?
Who owns the approval for repository access, and is it separate from the identity account?

cases.summary: Emergency elevation used during an incident; retrospective approval not evidenced
cases.notes: Emergency access is the path designed to bypass the approval gate. The elevation is confirmed in the system; the retrospective approval the standard requires has no record at all, and the removal has only an audit-log entry with no later observation. Both changes sit on ONE system, so each piece of evidence has to name which change it concerns -- evidence that does not is excluded as ambiguous rather than credited to whichever change is nearby.

access_changes.entitlement: emergency elevated role, after the incident

evidence.statement: A published standard requires retrospective approval of emergency elevation within one working day
Elevation recorded in the pipeline audit log
Role listing during the incident window shows the elevated role present
Pipeline audit log records the elevated role being removed after the incident

interview_prompts: What record is created when emergency elevation is used, and who reviews it?
Can you show the retrospective approval for the 12 August elevation?
How is the elevated role removed after the incident, and is its removal observed?

cases.summary: Departure where the only applicable evidence is the written standard
cases.notes: The refusal case. There is a policy and nothing else, so no conclusion about this departure can be drawn at all. The policy is not weak evidence here; it is evidence about a different subject.

evidence.statement: A published standard requires access removal on the last working day

interview_prompts: For a departure in May, what records would still exist today?
Where are offboarding tickets retained, and for how long?
If no ticket exists, is there any system-side record that would show when the account was disabled?

cases.summary: Departure where the system state contradicts the closed ticket, and a stale export was offered as proof
cases.notes: Two mechanisms at once. The reporting database still shows the account after the departure, which outranks the closed ticket. And an export taken before the departure was offered as evidence for the identity provider; it is excluded and listed, because it cannot show a later change.

evidence.statement: Offboarding ticket raised
Approved by the line manager
Directory export supplied as evidence of removal
Ticket closed, marked administrative role removed
Role listing still shows the administrative role assigned
A quarterly entitlement review was recorded in July

interview_prompts: The database still shows this role. Was the change reversed, never applied, or applied to a different account?
What date does the supplied directory export cover, and is there one from after the departure?
Does the quarterly entitlement review cover the reporting database's administrative roles?
